lab_title: Exploring VSEPR Theory: Molecular Geometry in 3D
top_level_objectives: Understand the principles of VSEPR theory and its role in predicting molecular shapes.
Identify and differentiate between the five fundamental electron-domain geometries.
Analyze how lone pairs affect molecular geometry and bond angles.

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce students to the concept of VSEPR theory, focusing on electron repulsion and molecular shapes.
key_visuals: Animated Lewis structure of a central atom with surrounding electron pairs
student_actions: Listen to an overview of VSEPR theory
Interact with the Lewis structure to identify bonding and lone pairs

scenes.brief_purpose: Demonstrate the five fundamental electron-domain geometries through interactive models.
key_visuals: 3D models of linear, trigonal planar, tetrahedral, trigonal bipyramidal, and octahedral geometries
student_actions: Rotate and manipulate 3D models to observe different electron-domain shapes
Place electron pairs around a central atom and witness the geometry formation

scenes.brief_purpose: Show how lone pairs alter the predicted molecular geometries.
key_visuals: Comparative models of shapes with and without lone pairs (e.g., methane vs. ammonia)
Highlighting lone pairs on interactive models
student_actions: Adjust lone pairs and observe changes in molecular shapes
Identify the resulting shapes like bent and trigonal pyramidal

scenes.brief_purpose: Compare VSEPR predictions against actual molecular structures in real-world molecules.
key_visuals: 3D representations of real molecules: water, ammonia, methane, PF5, SF6, XeF4
student_actions: Match predicted geometries with real molecular structures
Discuss the similarities and differences observed

scenes.brief_purpose: Explore why bond angles are slightly modified due to lone pairs occupying more space.
key_visuals: Visuals of molecular geometries with bond angles indicated
Graphs showing deviations in bond angles (e.g., 104.5° vs. 109.5°)
student_actions: Examine how lone pairs affect bond angles in various geometries
Calculate and compare the ideal vs. observed angles

scenes.brief_purpose: Summarize key takeaways from the lab and reinforce understanding of VSEPR theory.
key_visuals: Key concepts and summaries displayed in a visually engaging format
student_actions: Participate in a quiz based on lab content
Reflect on learning outcomes and ask questions
